question: Consider the following subsets of the plane: $C_1=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y=1/x\}$ and $C_2=\{(x,y):x<0,\ y=-1+1/x\}$. Given any two points $P=(x,y)$ and $Q=(u,v)$ of the plane, their distance is defined by $d(P,Q)=\sqrt{(x-u)^2+(y-v)^2}$. Show that there exists a unique choice of points $P_0\in C_1$ and $Q_0\in C_2$ such that $d(P_0,Q_0)\le d(P,Q)$ for all $P\in C_1$ and $Q\in C_2$.
